slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Was Jesus’s name predicted? Some translations say a ruler called “Shiloh” will come. The claim says Shiloh means “the one sent,” a title that points to Jesus.
slides.body: Some translations say a ruler called “Shiloh” will come. The claim says Shiloh means “the one sent,” a title that points to Jesus.
slides.heading: Was Jesus’s name predicted?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 49:10: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
slides.body: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
slides.heading: Gen 49:10

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 17:3, BSB: Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
slides.body: Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 17:3

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians connect them The verse can be read as promising a future ruler. Jesus repeatedly says God sent him, so “the one sent” sounds like a good match.
slides.body: The verse can be read as promising a future ruler. Jesus repeatedly says God sent him, so “the one sent” sounds like a good match.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But “sent” is not a secure meaning The Hebrew word is difficult, and many translations do not treat Shiloh as a name at all. John never calls Jesus Shiloh or says this verse predicted him.
slides.body: The Hebrew word is difficult, and many translations do not treat Shiloh as a name at all. John never calls Jesus Shiloh or says this verse predicted him.
slides.heading: But “sent” is not a secure meaning
